rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for excessive or insincere praise intended to please someone.

example.english: His flattery of the boss is clearly meant to win him a promotion.
example.traditional: 佢對老闆嘅奉承，明顯係想搏升職。
example.jyutping: keoi5 deoi3 lou5 baan2 ge3 fung6 sing4 ming4 hin2 hai6 soeng2 bok3 sing1 zik1

rows.note: Use this colloquial noun for clearly sycophantic flattery, especially when someone is trying to win favour.

example.english: You don't need so much flattery; you may not get the job anyway.
example.traditional: 你唔使拍咁多馬屁，份工都未必輪到你。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 sai2 paak3 gam3 do1 maa5 pei3 fan2 gung1 dou1 mei6 bit1 leon4 dou3 nei5

rows.note: Use this when the flattery is phrased as polite praise, though it can also be sincere rather than insincere.

example.english: Thanks for the flattery, but I’m really not as good as you say.
example.traditional: 多謝你嘅恭維，不過我真係冇你講得咁叻。
example.jyutping: do1 ze6 nei5 ge3 gung1 wai4 bat1 gwo3 ngo5 zan1 hai6 mou5 nei5 gong2 dak1 gam3 lek1
